purpose: The single decision that can make the independent-model gate meaningless. Frozen and hashed BEFORE any gate output is examined, so post-hoc tuning is detectable. Every value below is either read from a hash-pinned HotSpot input or derived from one by a stated identity. Nothing is fitted.

sources.note: The config/materials hashes are the ones the schema-5 manifest records for the staged inputs; the runner must re-verify them against the manifest, not against this file.
sources.read_from: artifacts_receipts/v61_cg5_schema5/v61_manifest.json input_hashes -- read programmatically, never transcribed. An earlier draft of this file carried two hashes I typed from a rendered document that shows only the first 16 characters and invented the remaining 48: correct prefix, correct length, valid hex, entirely fabricated. A prefix check would have passed them.

geometry.mesh_note: The 3D-ICE cell size is set to reproduce HotSpot's 64x64 grid over the same bounding box EXACTLY. This is what makes the observation operators comparable: with `output_quantity = MAXIMUM`, a floorplan element's reported temperature is the maximum over the cells covering it in both tools.
geometry.coverage: The 233 blocks cover all 4096 cells, so there is no whitespace requiring a material assignment. Verified geometrically in research/triangle/v61_tie_mechanism.py.
geometry.dram_placement: SAME LAYER, side by side. HotSpot models the DRAM dies as named blocks in the one floorplan, so a stacked interpretation would not be the instance being replicated. The four DRAM blocks sit at the chip corners.

die.source_note: Power is deposited in the silicon die layer, matching HotSpot, which has no separate source sublayer when a layer-configuration file is absent.

below_note: EMPTY, because the pinned config sets `-model_secondary 0`: no C4, underfill, package substrate or solder balls. This is a determination, not a choice.

boundary.derivation: HotSpot pins a TOTAL convective conductance 1/r_convec = 10.00 W/K. 3D-ICE applies an HTC over the chip footprint (389.447 mm^2), so HTC = (1/r_convec)/A_chip = 25677.4 W/(m^2 K). This preserves the heat path exactly.
boundary.rejected_alternative: Preserving HotSpot's HTC per unit area instead (1/(r_convec * A_sink) = 2777.8 W/(m^2 K)) would leave only 1.08 W/K of the 10.00 W/K path -- silently removing 90% of the cooling. Not defensible, and recorded here so the choice is visible.

known_structural_differences.detail: HotSpot carries a lumped sink capacitance c_convec = 140.4 J/K. Its time constant r*c = 14.04 s is about 35,000x the 0.4051 ms workload period, so over one cycle it behaves as a fixed reservoir -- which is exactly what 3D-ICE's fixed-ambient boundary already is.
known_structural_differences.affects: warm-up and absolute level, NOT the periodic uplift this gate measures

known_structural_differences.item: spreader and sink lateral footprint cannot be represented
known_structural_differences.detail: HotSpot's spreader is 50 mm and its sink 60 mm square -- 6.4x and 9.2x the chip footprint -- while 3D-ICE passive layers share the chip footprint. Lateral spreading beyond the die is therefore absent, which biases 3D-ICE HOTTER.
known_structural_differences.affects: absolute level, and the vertical thermal mass seen over one cycle
known_structural_differences.consequence: this is the robustness set below

robustness_set.why: One genuinely admissible modelling choice remains, so per the preregistration's guard a positive verdict requires BOTH members to reproduce; otherwise the outcome is MAPPING_SENSITIVE/UNRESOLVED. They are run as a set, never in sequence until one reproduces the flip.

members.description: TIM + spreader + sink as explicit chip-footprint passive layers above the die, with the derived HTC at the top boundary. Keeps the vertical thermal mass of the copper.

TIM only, with spreader and sink folded into the top boundary condition at the same total conductance. Removes the copper's vertical thermal mass, which is the part that can change a sub-millisecond uplift.

numerics.integration_step_s: matched to the HotSpot replay step via rte's exact Fraction timing
numerics.resolution_note: 3D-ICE reports to 0.001 K, ten times finer than HotSpot's 0.01 K. The interval [X_L, X_U] for each observable must still include this quantisation, per the preregistration.
numerics.timestep_sequence: the matched step, then half it, for closure
numerics.periodic_closure: cycle doubling until the boundary and peak residuals fall within the reported resolution, the same criterion CertiTherm.transient uses
numerics.output_quantity_note: ThreeDiceOutputQuantity.MAXIMUM, chosen so the reported element temperature is a maximum over covering cells as in HotSpot's grid_map_mode=max. AVERAGE would be a different observation operator and would not be comparable.

prohibitions: No fitted power, temperature, conductance, convection or geometric calibration.
POWER_SCALE is 1 by construction. Unit conversion (W/m-K to W/um-K, J/m^3-K to J/um^3-K) is not calibration.
No change to any value here after gate output is examined, except as a newly declared preregistered attempt with its own hash.
